statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Name Reservation and Company Register (app.companiesoffice.govt.nz and register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must use Latin script; Te Reo Maori macron diacritics are accepted; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into an approved Latin-alphabet form. The name must include a distinctive element and must end with 'Limited' (or an approved Maori equivalent where permitted by the Companies Office).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is not renewable after the 20-working-day validity period. If the Registrar refuses a name, written reasons must be requested from the Companies Office; an administrative reconsideration submission should be filed within 10 working days, accompanied by statutory arguments under Companies Act 1993 sections 22-24 and any consent letters from affected professional or governmental bodies. If the refusal is sustained, the applicant may seek judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible as a registered office only if it is a physical street address in New Zealand at which legal documents may be served during normal business hours and a responsible natural person is present for acceptance of service. A post-office box address is not acceptable. The Specialty Tea Salon and Cultural Ceramic Lounge must in all cases occupy a real, licensable trading premises for the food and beverage activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: moderate-to-high for the trading premises because the Food Act 2014 requires registration with a territorial authority and risk-based unannounced inspections by local council or Ministry for Primary Industries verifiers, with an estimated 35%-60% probability within the first operating year; low risk (under 5%) for unannounced Companies Office inspection of the registered office unless a compliance complaint is received.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (New Zealand), sections 12-16 (registration of companies), sections 20-24 (company name rules), sections 151-159 (director eligibility and residency), sections 161-165 (registered office and address for service), sections 65-96 (share issues, allotment and registers); Financial Reporting Act 2013; Companies (Fees) Regulations 2010; Tax Administration Act 1994 and Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 for ancillary tax registration
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, an operational business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation, and Employment (MBIE), acting through the Registrar of Companies
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 - Application for Incorporation, electronically lodged through the official New Zealand Companies Office online register (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital requirement is imposed by the Companies Act 1993. The International Company (CK_IC) may be incorporated with a nominal issued capital of NZ$1.00 and paid-up capital may be deferred until share allotment. No escrow account is statutorily mandated; however, if subscription funds are collected prior to allotment, they must be held in a segregated client funds account at an authorised New Zealand bank. Where shares are issued at a premium, the premium amount must be credited to a share premium account subject to the distribution restrictions in section 55 of the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] INTERNATIONAL COMPANY LIMITED, adopted by unanimous written resolution of the founding directors and shareholder on [DATE], pursuant to section 122 of the Companies Act 1993. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED that the board accept the share subscription applications tendered by the founding shareholders for [NUMBER] ordinary shares of NZ$[PAR VALUE] each, allot such shares forthwith, record the allotment in the register of members in accordance with sections 87 and 88 of the Companies Act 1993, and deposit all subscription monies into the company's corporate bank account maintained at an authorised New Zealand bank. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED that the statutory registered office of the company be established and fixed at [PHYSICAL STREET ADDRESS, CITY, NEW ZEALAND], and that such office be maintained accessible to the public and for the service of process during ordinary business hours in accordance with sections 161 and 193 of the Companies Act 1993. 3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED that [FULL NAME 1] be and is hereby appointed as Managing Director, [FULL NAME 2] be and is hereby appointed as Director, and [FULL NAME 3] be and is hereby appointed as Company Secretary, each to hold office subject to the company constitution and the Companies Act 1993; and that the designated compliance officer be charged with overseeing the Food Act 2014 registration, the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 obligations, and all Inland Revenue and Companies Office filings. 4. GENERAL AND OPERATIONAL AUTHORITY: RESOLVED that the Managing Director and Company Secretary be jointly and severally authorised to negotiate and execute the lease of the specialty tea salon lounge premises located at [PREMISES ADDRESS], to engage licensed legal and accounting advisers, to open corporate bank and merchant card accounts, to procure public liability and fire insurance, and to complete all ancillary applications with Fire and Emergency New Zealand, the territorial authority, and the Ministry for Primary Industries.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Pre-Incorporation Governance Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Online Name Availability and Reservation Portal (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a comprehensive name availability search against the Companies Office register, the New Zealand Intellectual Property Office trade mark database, and common-law usage records. Submit a request to reserve the proposed company name '[COMPANY NAME] INTERNATIONAL COMPANY LIMITED' and, where the name contains a restricted word (e.g., 'Bank', 'Trust', 'University'), obtain the written consent of the relevant sector regulator under section 21 of the Companies Act 1993. Verify that the proposed name is not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered name and is not otherwise objectionable under section 20. Finalize the pre-incorporation governance checklist, including director and shareholder identity verification and conflict-of-interest declarations.
required_dossiers: Name availability search report obtained from the Companies Office register
Proposed company name reservation application signed by the incorporating agent
Written consent from the relevant regulator if a restricted word is included
Certified passport copies and proof of residential address for each founding director and shareholder
Pre-incorporation conflict-of-interest and governance checklist
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the applicant may file a formal written objection with the Registrar of Companies, procure the consent of the relevant sector regulator, or elect an alternative approved name and continue the incorporation without loss of priority. A name refusal does not invalidate the incorporation application if a different compliant name is substituted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgment of Form 1 - Application for Incorporation and Statutory Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Official Electronic Filing System (MBIE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and electronically lodge Form 1 with the New Zealand Companies Office, stating the company name, the physical New Zealand registered office address, the address for service, the full legal names and residential addresses of all directors and shareholders, the share structure (class, number, nominal value, and voting rights), and the company constitution (whether the default constitution under section 18 or a custom constitution). Upload executed consent-to-act forms for each director, verify all particulars by digital attestation, and remit the statutory filing fee of NZ$150.00 (approximately USD 95.00) through the online payment gateway. Upon successful lodgment, the register automatically allocates a company number and a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
required_dossiers: Form 1 - Application for Incorporation fully executed
Written consent to appointment executed by each director
Certified passport copies and address verification for each director and shareholder
Company constitution (custom or confirmation of section 18 default application)
Evidence of the physical registered office address (lease, tenancy agreement, or title deed)
Incorporation fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice of intention to decline under section 13(2) of the Companies Act 1993, the applicant has 20 working days to submit supplementary evidence curing the defect, including corrected name searches, compliant registered office documentation, or director eligibility certificates. If the application is formally declined, a fresh application may be filed with a new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Establishment of Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Office of the Registrar of Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of the incorporation application, the electronic Certificate of Incorporation is generated automatically. Verify the registration date, company number, NZBN, and registered office as displayed on the public register. Download and permanently archive the certificate, and open the company's statutory records, including the register of members, register of directors, minute book, and register of charges, at the registered office or at a licensed corporate secretarial service provider in New Zealand. Obtain a corporate bank account mandate using the certificate and NZBN.
required_dossiers: Electronic Certificate of Incorporation downloaded from the Companies Office register
Company constitution and register extract of incorporation particulars
Board resolution appointing the corporate secretary and records administrator
Corporate bank account opening application and mandate
Registered office acceptance letter from the corporate secretarial provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed or contains clerical errors, submit a written correction request to the Registrar under sections 15 and 16 of the Companies Act 1993, or escalate through the MBIE Companies Office service desk. Any discrepancy between the certificate and the intended share structure is cured by a supplementary filing and an amended certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Resolution, Share Allotment, and Officer Appointment Recordal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company board of directors acting under the Companies Act 1993; notifications lodged with the New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the inaugural board meeting or execute a unanimous written resolution adopting the pro-forma first board resolution. Allot the founding ordinary shares to the subscribers, issue share certificates, and record the allotment in the register of members. If the issued capital changes, lodge Form 5 (Return of Allotment) with the Companies Office within 10 business days. Formalize the appointments of the Managing Director, Director, and Company Secretary, and record the appointments in the Companies Office register. Ensure that at least one director is a New Zealand resident or that a registered agent is appointed in accordance with section 151 of the Companies Act 1993.
required_dossiers: First board resolution adopted in accordance with section 122 of the Companies Act 1993
Share application forms and letters of allotment for each founding subscriber
Share certificates for the issued ordinary shares
Form 5 - Return of Allotment (where the allotment is made)
Signed letters of appointment and consents of each director and the company secretary
Register of directors and register of members updated to the date of the meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an allotment or officer appointment is queried by the Companies Office, a third party, or the Registrar, the board may pass a ratifying resolution, amend the share register under section 95 of the Companies Act 1993, and re-file the corrected statutory forms. If director eligibility is contested, appoint an alternate director satisfying the residency or agent requirements and notify the Registrar promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office and Address for Service Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office - Official Register Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the registered office is a physical location in New Zealand that is open to the public for at least 20 hours per week and available for service of documents and statutory inspections, as required by section 161 of the Companies Act 1993. File Form 6 (Notice of Registered Office) and Form 7 (Notice of Address for Service) with the Companies Office, and ensure the registered office and address for service are maintained continuously; any change must be filed within 10 working days.
required_dossiers: Form 6 - Notice of Registered Office duly executed
Form 7 - Notice of Address for Service duly executed
Lease deed, service office agreement, or proof of ownership of the physical registered office in New Zealand
Acceptance letter from the registered office service provider
Board resolution approving the registered office and address for service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office determines that the registered office is not a genuine physical place open during business hours, it will serve a notice of non-compliance requiring rectification. The company must promptly secure a compliant street address, file the updated Form 6 and Form 7, and pay any late-filing penalty. Continued non-compliance may expose the company to strike-off under section 318 of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inland Revenue Registration - IRD Number, GST, PAYE, and Tax Classification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue New Zealand (Inland Revenue Department)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a New Zealand IRD number using the IR742 company registration form or through the Inland Revenue online services portal, attaching the Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN confirmation. Register for Goods and Services Tax under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 if projected annual taxable supplies exceed NZ$60,000, or elect voluntary GST registration to claim input credits on premises fit-out and commercial lease costs. If the specialty tea salon will employ staff, register as an employer for PAYE and obtain a KiwiSaver deduction schedule. Confirm the company's non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) obligations on any distributions to foreign shareholders and maintain the company's tax residence documentation.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN confirmation
IR742 company registration and tax classification form
GST registration application and projected turnover declaration
PAYE employer registration schedule and KiwiSaver election
Board resolution appointing the tax compliance officer and confirming bank account details
Ownership and director particulars for NRWT and beneficial ownership records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Inland Revenue queries the tax registration, the company must respond within 28 days with the certificate of incorporation, director identities, and New Zealand registered office evidence. If late-filing or late-payment penalties arise, the company may file a penalty mitigation request under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and apply to reschedule provisional tax instalments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Control Plan Registration and Territorial Authority Operational Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry for Primary Industries (New Zealand Food Safety) and the relevant territorial authority (city or district council environmental health department)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Develop and implement a written Food Control Plan (FCP) under the Food Act 2014 that addresses loose-leaf tea receiving and storage, brewing and water quality, ceramic service ware sanitation, allergen declaration, temperature control, and traceability. Submit the FCP and premises details through the MPI Food Registration online portal, pay the applicable registration fee, and obtain the Certified Food Premises registration certificate. Coordinate with the territorial authority's environmental health officer for a pre-opening inspection of the tea salon lounge, including sighting of the tea service counter, kitchenette, scullery, and hand-washing facilities. Display the food business registration certificate on the premises before commencing trade.
required_dossiers: Food Control Plan (FCP) with HACCP-based risk matrix and critical control points
MPI online food business registration application (Form 606 or electronic equivalent)
Detailed premises floor plan and plumbing and ventilation schedule
Potable water supply test certificate and water heater compliance certificate
Certificate of analysis for all tea blends and allergen declaration records
Pre-opening environmental health inspection report and council fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Food Control Plan registration is refused or conditioned, the operator may submit a revised FCP addressing the inspection findings, request a risk assessment variation, or appeal to the New Zealand Food Safety registrar. A temporary food business registration may be granted pending final approval, and all non-compliant items identified by the council inspector must be remediated before the certificate is uplifted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: New Zealand Food Safety (Ministry for Primary Industries) in conjunction with the territorial authority (city or district council environmental health and building inspection departments); Fire and Emergency New Zealand for fire safety certification; regional council under the Resource Management Act 1991 for trade-waste discharge and environmental permitting
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registered Food Control Plan (Food Act 2014) - Food Business Registration and Certified Food Premises Certificate; Food and Beverage Service Operational Licence; Building Warrant of Fitness (BWoF) with Compliance Schedule under the Building Act 2004; optional on-licence under the Sale and Supply of Alcohol Act 2012 if tea-infused alcoholic preparations are served

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) New Zealand and the applicable regional council acting as the Resource Management Act 1991 consent authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 3 - Permitted Activity / Registration tier; no full Environmental Impact Assessment report is required for an indoor specialty tea salon lounge, but a low-impact activity registration and trade-waste discharge approval from the regional council or territorial authority is a mandatory precondition to operation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Liquid trade waste discharged from the tea salon must comply with the regional council's trade-waste bylaw, including pH within 6.0-10.0, total suspended solids not exceeding 300 mg/L, oil and grease not exceeding 100 mg/L, and a maximum wastewater temperature of 40 degrees Celsius at the boundary of the discharge. Kitchen and salon ventilation and exhaust systems must meet AS/NZS 1668.1 air-handling code requirements; odour, volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and particulate emissions must remain below the National Environmental Standard for Air Quality (NES-AQ) thresholds, including PM10 at 50 ug/m3 measured as a 24-hour average and PM2.5 at 25 ug/m3 annual average. Noise emissions from service activities and ventilation equipment must not exceed 50 dB(A) L10 at the property boundary during night hours under NZS 6802:2008 and section 16 of the Resource Management Act 1991. Solid waste including spent tea leaf residue and ceramic packaging must be segregated for recycling or commercial composting and collected by a licensed waste carrier under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and an approved evacuation scheme must be obtained from Fire and Emergency New Zealand (FENZ) under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017, including fire-rated separations for the tea bar kitchenette and ceramic display areas. A Building Warrant of Fitness (BWoF) with an annual Form 12A inspection certificate and structural load assessment for the salon mezzanine and tea service counter must be maintained under sections 168-169 of the Building Act 2004. Occupational health and workplace clearance must be established under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including a documented hazard register, first-aid kits, fire extinguisher placement, electrical tag-and-test certificates for all tea brewing equipment, and a staff induction and training record. A civil defence and earthquake emergency preparedness plan must be registered with the relevant regional Civil Defence Emergency Management group, including structural bracing checks for shelving and ceramic displays and a post-earthquake gas and water isolation protocol.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Te Tari Tāke) via the myIR secure online portal; customs export administration by the New Zealand Customs Service
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-incorporated International Company (CK_IC) holding a Speciality Tea Salon/Lounge operation in New Zealand: (1) register the overseas company with the New Zealand Companies Office and obtain a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN); (2) apply to Inland Revenue for a non-individual IRD number, providing the certificate of incorporation and good standing, registered office address, New Zealand address for service, details of directors, shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners, and a statutory declaration on the place of central management and control; (3) use the issued IRD number as the single statutory TIN for income tax, GST and employer obligations, as no separate VAT identifier exists; (4) register for GST in myIR as soon as taxable supplies in New Zealand reach or are expected to exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period, or voluntarily if the company wishes to claim input tax credits while exporting; and (5) file the relevant New Zealand income tax return for any fixed establishment or, if no New Zealand taxable presence exists, file a non-resident disclosure confirming that no New Zealand tax return is required. The Cook Islands tax-exempt-zone status does not displace these New Zealand registration obligations where a New Zealand fixed establishment or taxable activity exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not maintain a US-style check-the-box election. The CK_IC International Company is classified under New Zealand law as a non-resident company unless its central management and control is exercised in New Zealand; the Cook Islands tax-exempt status does not confer a New Zealand income tax exemption. Available elections are limited to voluntary GST registration before the compulsory threshold is reached and GST group registration under section 55 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. Hybrid and branch mismatch rules are mandatory, so no elective hybrid-mismatch carve-out may be asserted to avoid a New Zealand tax adjustment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST), a value-added-type consumption tax administered under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in a rolling 12-month period; compulsory registration applies when the threshold is exceeded, including supplies made by a non-resident supplier of remote services to New Zealand consumers where the threshold is met.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand has no real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory digital stamping, and no API-based government pre-authorisation for GST invoices. E-invoicing is voluntary under the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 four-corner model recognised by Inland Revenue. All GST invoices must contain the statutory content, including supplier identity, IRD number, GST-inclusive amount and supply date, and must be retained in a readable electronic or paper format. GST returns are filed electronically through myIR; no invoice-level clearance code is required for a valid invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% applies to goods physically exported from New Zealand by or on behalf of the supplier, and to services supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand when the direct benefit of the services is enjoyed outside New Zealand. For the Speciality Tea Salon/Lounge, eligible zero-rated exports include loose-leaf tea, high-end tea ware and ceramic products sent to overseas customers, as well as related remote consulting or cataloguing services provided to foreign buyers. Domestic supplies of prepared tea beverages, food for immediate consumption in the lounge, and serving of tea with hospitality services are standard-rated at 15%; packaged retail supplies of loose-leaf tea for home consumption may qualify for zero-rating as basic food when not supplied as part of a meal, restaurant or takeaway supply. A GST-registered exporter may claim input tax credits attributable to zero-rated exports and may obtain repayment of any resulting credit balance through its GST return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration lodged with the New Zealand Customs Service and the official exit confirmation report
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export from New Zealand
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank/FX records evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Supplier GST tax invoice and packing list
Export sales contract, purchase order and correspondence with the overseas buyer
Foreign-destination delivery or warehouse receipt where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may disallow zero-rating and retrospectively reassert output tax at 15% if the export documentation is incomplete, the goods did not in fact leave New Zealand, or export proceeds were not received or repatriated within the 180-day compliance window. Reassessment runs from the original supply date and carries use-of-money interest. Shortfall penalties apply under the Tax Administration Act 1994 at 150% for evasion or a similar act, 100% for an abusive tax position, 40% for gross carelessness and 20% for an unacceptable tax position. The ordinary four-year time bar does not apply where fraud or evasion is established, and criminal prosecution may result in fines and imprisonment. False export entries are also separately penalisable under New Zealand customs legislation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand – Te Pūtea Matua
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The New Zealand dollar (NZD) enjoys full convertibility across both current and capital account transactions under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's liberalised foreign exchange framework. There are no general exchange control approvals required for capital inflows or outflows, nor for the remittance of dividends, branch profits, or royalty payments. The External Investment Act and the Overseas Investment Act only impose screening requirements for certain large or sensitive asset acquisitions, not for routine operating capital or trade flows. A specialty tea salon undertaking normal commercial activities (lease, inventory, equipment) is not expected to encounter capital account hurdles, provided all tax liabilities, including non-resident withholding tax on dividends and interest, are duly settled.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no mandatory export proceeds surrender or conversion requirements. Exporters of tea, ceramics, or any other goods are free to receive foreign currency, retain it in foreign-currency bank accounts offshore or onshore, or convert it to NZD at commercial rates without a statutory timeline. The only obligation is accurate reporting of export income for income tax purposes and, where applicable, the OECD CRS and FATCA information reporting frameworks. No ratio of mandatory conversion exists.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for ancillary payment processing, Low-Medium as a primary treasury account. Offshore digital EMTs (e-money institutions) are generally permitted to offer payment services in New Zealand only if registered as a Financial Service Provider (FSP) under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and enrolled with an approved dispute resolution scheme. Additionally, the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 requires a licensed AML/CFT reporting entity with supervision from the Department of Internal Affairs. Global EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, and OFX operate through New Zealand bank partnerships or hold FSP status; however, they typically do not provide formal 'Capital Escrow' capacity, and rely on pass-through accounts with local banks, codifying a risk of settlement delay. For treasury-grade liquidity management and the holding of capital reserves, a direct account with a tier-1 domestic commercial bank is strongly recommended; EMIs should be annexed only for low-value cross-border disbursements where speed and FX rate efficiency are critical.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Regardless of whether the International Company is registered as a New Zealand resident entity or an overseas carry-on business, directors may generally complete onboarding remotely using certified copies of passports, proof of address, and a video identification interview with a bank-approved verifier. In practice, most tier-1 NZ banks require the company to hold a registered office or local service address in New Zealand and may require the ultimate beneficial owner to appear by video or, in certain cases, attend a branch or the local embassy for physical identification if the risk assessment flags geopolitical or high-risk jurisdictions. Cook Islands International Company (CK_IC) structures without a New Zealand Director may trigger a heightened risk rating; however, a smooth remote onboarding is achievable if all corporate record books, certificates of good standing, and a signed director resolution for the NZ account approval are produced with notarisation/apostille.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) residency without a verifiable physical footprint in New Zealand and no Director of New Zealand domicile
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised certificate of good standing for the CK_IC; apostilled memorandum and articles of association; full chain of ownership from the registered agent through each intermediate entity to the natural persons; bank statements of each owning entity for a 24-month period; a statutory declaration signed by all UBOs attesting to source of wealth and source of funds; and an irrevocable undertaking to appoint a New Zealand-resident agent for service of process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection from a Cook Islands trust or fiduciary arrangement that obscures principal identity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal trust deed (apostilled); a letter of inescrow engagement from the licensed trust company or registered trustee clearly identifying the settlor and protector; HSBC/Swiss/other reputable bank reference letter covering the trust’s account conduct; the trust’s audited financial statements or a solvency letter from a recognised audit firm; and an independent legal opinion confirming the trust is not a fictitious arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business nature as a hospitality/cash-intensive retail lounge increasing inconsistent cash transactions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan including POS terminal agreements and an acquirer agreement; franchise or lease agreement for the tea salon premises; supplier invoices for high-end tea stock and ceramic tableware; proposed daily cash/EFTPOS reconciliation protocol; and a commitment letter for using a certified accounting system with real-time cloud reporting.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade settlement with overseas suppliers in jurisdictions considered high-risk or having non-standard VAT/customs treatment (e.g., pottery imports from Asia)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authenticated supplier registration documents and trade licences; full commercial invoice, packing list, procurement contract, and bill of lading or airway bill per shipment; bank proof of payment history to the same supplier; and a customs broker’s guarantee that all NZ import duties and GST are paid before release.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The compliant routing for inbound equity injection or shareholder loans into a New Zealand operating company is a SWIFT MT103 (wire transfer) from the beneficial owner’s bank to the two designated accounts: (i) a NZD denominated capital escrow account for the FDI equity contribution, and (ii) an NZD operational account for intercompany loans / working capital. The remittance must clearly state the ISO 20022 structured purpose code and a supporting narrative. For equity injection, use the Economic Transaction Code (ETC) 1110 for inward direct investment (equity capital) and append the phrase 'Contribution to paid-in capital – CK_IC International Company'; for intercompany loans use ETC 1120. The inward remittance should be pre-advised to the relationship manager 48 business hours ahead. The bank will request the underlying corporate resolution, share allotment documentation, or loan agreement to complete the 'source of funds' verification, and to confirm the capital is not tied to foreign exchange restrictions. For amounts exceeding NZD 1 million, a certificate from a New Zealand chartered accountant on the non-manipulation of transfer pricing may be required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For high-value and supply-chain-sensitive trade settlements (e.g., bulk tea auctions or ceramic container imports), the preferred clearing rail is a SWIFT MT103 (for straight commercial payments) or a letter of credit (LC) issued under UCP600 terms (for deferred payment assurance). The treasury shall maintain a dual-track disbursement policy: for amounts under NZD 50,000, use SWIFT MT103 with immediate execution and verified beneficiary identifiers (BIC/IBAN); for amounts above NZD 50,000 or involving a new supplier, use an Irrevocable Confirmed Commercial LC. All outward transfers must be tagged with the appropriate transaction narrative (e.g., 'Trade Payment – Import of Tea Leaves – Inv. TSL-2024-1123') and the corresponding outward ETC codes. To reduce settlement risk, settlement shall be executed via the New Zealand Electronic Settlement System (ESAS) for same-day NZD clearing or via the correspondent bank’s SWIFT network for cross-currency. The relationship bank must receive a copy of the supplier’s beneficial ownership declaration if the payment is directed to a jurisdiction listed by the Financial Action Task Force as high-risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward contracts (NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/CNY, NZD/AUD) with a licensed New Zealand bank under the ISDA New Zealand Addendum and Financial Markets Conduct Act compliance
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic currency pairs where illiquid convertible currencies are traded against NZD, settled in NZD
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for converting a foreign currency capital injection into NZD liabilities or for managing longer-term currency mismatches
FX options (European style, plain-vanilla caps and floors) for income stream hedges without removing upside
Short-term money market deposits denominated in NZD and corresponding foreign currencies for interest-rate hedge arbitrage, matched to trade payable cycles

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 working days after the annual return date, being the last day of the month containing the anniversary of incorporation; initial return due 18 months after incorporation, then annually on the same anniversary cycle.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 100 (approx. USD 61) applies; continued non-filing after Registrar reminder triggers notice of proposed removal and strike-off from the New Zealand Register under s 319 of the Companies Act 1993.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Director Confirmation of Register Accuracy (Companies Office confirmation statement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies, MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during the company's confirmation month, aligned with the annual return filing window; confirmation must be completed before or concurrently with the Annual Return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No separate fee; failure to confirm director, shareholder, and registered-office details blocks completion of the annual filing cycle and may result in Registrar deregistration action for persistent default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements Filing (audited, where statutory threshold triggered)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies, MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements, where required for a large or shareholder-requisitioned company, must be filed with the Companies Office within 20 working days after board approval and before lodgement of the Annual Return; small exempt companies have no filing unless a 5%-shareholder audit requisition is served.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Offence under s 373 of the Companies Act 1993; fines of up to NZD 5,000 (approx. USD 3,000) plus continuing daily penalties, and the Registrar may commence strike-off proceedings for sustained non-delivery.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No independent audit is compulsory for a small New Zealand company (total assets not exceeding NZD 60 million and total revenue not exceeding NZD 30 million). A mandatory audit applies where the company qualifies as large, is an FMC-reporting entity, or where shareholders holding at least 5% of voting rights validly requisition an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Financial Reporting Act 2013 and External Reporting Board (XRB) standards: NZ IFRS (Tier 1) for large or public-accountability entities, Tier 2 reduced-disclosure NZ IFRS, and Tier 3 Simple Format Reporting Accounting (SFR-A) for small non-issuer entities; books may be maintained in NZD or the company's elected functional currency.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a standalone UBO register; ultimate beneficial ownership is captured through the annual director confirmation certifying the accuracy of shareholding data on the Companies Register. Each share transfer or allotment is recorded immediately in the Register of Members and electronically notified to the Companies Office within 15 working days of the transaction; the annual confirmation cycle memorialises the post-transaction ownership composition.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (including consents and director interests)
Minute Book (board and shareholder meeting minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 9,000 (NZD 5,000 – NZD 15,000) when an audit is formally requisitioned; generally not incurred for an exempt small company.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or preferential corporate rates are available in New Zealand. The standard 28% corporate rate applies to all net taxable income. A Cook Islands International Company (CK_IC) with a 'Tax-Exempt Zone' status enjoys no New Zealand exemption; NZ-source income (e.g., retail tea sales, service fees, royalties, or branch profits) is fully subject to NZ income tax at 28%. The Research and Development Tax Incentive (15% credit) and loss carry-back provisions are generally irrelevant to specialty tea salon/lounge operations. No regional or industry-specific tax holidays are granted.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory 5-year expiry; indefinite carryforward is available under the Income Tax Act 2007 s IA 2, subject to the 49% continuity of beneficial ownership test and, for non-resident companies, the same business test under s IA 5)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 — Income Tax Return for Companies; filed electronically through Inland Revenue's myIR portal or approved tax preparation software (SAFE / e-File). GST returns (GST101) and employer obligations (IR348/ER348) are filed separately through myIR.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual income tax return. Provisional tax is paid in three instalments during the year; GST is filed monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly depending on turnover; PAYE/FBT filings are monthly/annually.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date: the IR4 return and terminal tax payment are due 7 July immediately following the income year; a tax agent holding an extension of time may file by 31 March of the following year (e.g., year ended 31 March 2025 extended to 31 March 2026). Terminal tax on its own is due 7 April (or 7 May with a tax agent). Provisional tax instalments fall on 28 August, 15 January, and 7 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income: gross sales and revenue from specialty tea salon/lounge operations, including retail loose-leaf tea, prepared beverages, food service, cultural ceramic sales, and any online/DTC sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the CK_IC is a non-resident company operating in NZ solely through a fixed establishment, include only NZ-sourced income attributable to that establishment. Exclude foreign-source income unless the company is NZ tax resident by incorporation or centre of management.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income (sum of all income lines, including interest, dividends, royalties, and other assessable income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident CK_IC must report all New Zealand-sourced business income attributable to the NZ permanent establishment; add back any adjustments required by transfer pricing rules under s GC 13–GC 14 of the Income Tax Act 2007.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses: allowable deductions including cost of tea leaf imports, rent, wages, depreciation, freight, packaging, marketing, and administrative overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses incurred in deriving NZ-source income. Head office costs must be apportioned on an arm's length basis; any intra-group management fees must be supported by transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss (total income less total expenses).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The result must reflect the profits that would have been earned by an independent enterprise performing identical activities; a tax-exempt IC cannot use its offshore exempt status to erode the NZ branch profit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Losses carried forward: prior-year net losses available to offset current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Available only if the 49% continuity of beneficial ownership test is satisfied. For a CK_IC with fluctuating shareholders, or if the beneficial owner changes, the loss balance is forfeited; attach ownership continuity schedules if reviewed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after application of loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a branch of a non-resident, use the adjusted taxable income as computed after transfer pricing corrections; any unnecessary shift of profit to a tax-exempt head office will be disregarded by Inland Revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax on taxable income at the 28% flat corporate rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 28% to the net taxable income; no progressive rates or separate non-resident corporate rate exists. The 'Tax-Exempt Zone' status of a foreign IC has no effect on the NZ-sourced portion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: imputation credits attached to NZ dividends received, resident withholding tax (RWT) credits, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident company may only claim RWT/NRWT credits in respect of NZ-source dividends or interest; foreign tax credits are available only if the income is also assessable in NZ and a DTA arrangement applies. Do not claim imputation credits if no imputation account has been maintained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net tax payable or refund due after all credits and provisional tax payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any balance due is payable on the terminal tax date; late payment triggers monthly penalties and Use of Money Interest. A refund is issued only after Inland Revenue verifies the non-resident's NZ tax position.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties for IR4: NZ$50 for the first month, NZ$250 for the second month, and NZ$500 for the third and each subsequent month. Late payment penalties: 1% immediate, plus 4% after 7 days, and 1% per month thereafter. Use of Money Interest (UOMI) accrues daily at the prescribed rate (currently 8.92% per annum for underpayments as of Q3 2025). Shortfall penalties for incorrect returns: 20% (failure to take reasonable care), 40% (unacceptable tax position), 100% (abusive tax position), and 150% (evasion). A non-filer assessment under s 106 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 imposes a 20% shortfall penalty on the assessed tax plus all late filing penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% (Non-Resident Withholding Tax, NRWT) on dividends paid by a NZ-resident company to non-resident shareholders. Fully imputed dividends paid to an Australian-resident company under the trans-Tasman imputation rules are exempt at 0%. Under most NZ DTAs the rate is reduced to 15% for portfolio dividends and 0%–5% for substantial corporate shareholders (10%+ voting interest).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief on dividends, interest, or royalties from New Zealand: (1) the non-resident beneficial owner must provide the NZ payer with a completed IR3NR 'Non-Resident Withholding Tax Declaration' (or IRD-approved digital equivalent) stating the treaty country of residence; (2) the beneficial owner must obtain and furnish a valid Certificate of Residence (CoR) from its home country tax authority, confirming residence for tax purposes and, where the DTA contains a Limitation on Benefits or Principal Purpose Test, evidencing entitlement to treaty benefits; (3) the NZ payer then withholds at the reduced DTA rate. If the CoR is not provided, the statutory NRWT rates apply (30% dividends; 15% interest/royalties), and the recipient must file an application for refund or treaty relief (Form IR370) within the statute-bar period (generally four years from the end of the income year). The IR3NR declaration must be renewed at least every three years or on any material change of circumstances.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on royalties is 15% (Income Tax Act 2007 s RF 2); statutory NRWT on interest is 15%; the Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% may apply to interest paid to an unrelated non-resident lender (where no associated-person loan). DTA rates commonly found: interest — 10% (Australia, US, UK, Japan, Singapore, Hong Kong SAR DTA); royalties — 5% for copyright/patent rights and 10% for other royalties under the NZ-US DTA; NZ-Australia DTA royalties 5%; NZ-Japan DTA royalties 10%. The tea salon must apply these rates only after receiving the IR3NR and CoR; otherwise statutory rates apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory where aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed NZ$3 million in an income year (Inland Revenue Transfer Pricing Guidelines 2020; Income Tax Act 2007 s GC 13). Master File and Country-by-Country Report: mandatory where the multinational group has consolidated group revenue of NZ$1.12 billion or more. Detailed contemporaneous documentation is also required for any cross-border financing, royalty, or management fee arrangement with a related party regardless of size if it materially affects NZ taxable income.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code (as in BVI/Cayman). However, economic substance is enforced through: (i) the general anti-avoidance rule (s BG 1/GB 1 Income Tax Act 2007), which voids any arrangement with a tax avoidance purpose lacking commercial reality; (ii) transfer pricing rules under s GC 13–GC 14; (iii) thin capitalisation rules under s FE 2–FE 18 for foreign-owned entities; and (iv) the Principal Purpose Test in NZ DTAs under the MLI. A 'Tax-Exempt Zone' CK_IC with no physical presence, staff, active decision-making, or real economic activity in its home jurisdiction that purports to hold the NZ tea salon's IP or finance will be re-characterised: Inland Revenue will deem the company to be NZ tax resident if its centre of management is in NZ (s YD 2(1)(c)) and assess its worldwide income at 28%; alternatively the arrangement will be treated as a sham with profits assessed to the actual NZ operators.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly providing false information in an IR4 return, understating cash sales from the specialty tea salon, creating fictitious supplier invoices for purportedly imported ceramic tea ware, backdating or forging GST/NRWT records, or deliberately omitting NZ-source income earned through the tea lounge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under s 143A of the Tax Administration Act 1994: a fine of up to NZ$50,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 5 years per offence. In addition, a civil shortfall penalty of 150% of the tax shortfall applies for evasion, plus full payment of unpaid tax and Use of Money Interest. Under the Proceeds of Crime Act 2009, asset confiscation orders may strip the value of the tea salon business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns, direct the under-reporting, or who knowingly benefit from fraudulent invoicing are guilty as parties to the offence and face the same imprisonment and fines. Under the Tax Administration Act 1994 s 372, directors are personally liable for unpaid PAYE/GST deductions and for any penalty arising from their own actions. Reckless trading under s 289 Companies Act 1993 exposes directors to personal civil liability for the company's tax debts. Travel restrictions are typically imposed as bail conditions (passport surrender, Customs departure bans) once criminal charges are laid; serious fraud prosecutions may be accompanied by a Proceeds of Crime restraint order freezing personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the 'Tax-Exempt Zone' CK_IC structure as a shell to strip taxable profit from the profitable NZ tea salon through inflated intercompany management fees, excessive royalty charges for a worthless brand, or uncommercial back-to-back loans with high interest, while maintaining no real substance in the Cook Islands and no arm's length documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The general anti-avoidance rule under s BG 1/GB 1 disregards the arrangement and reconstructs the income on the NZ operator; a shortfall penalty of 100% of the tax shortfall applies for an abusive tax position (s 141D). The promoter penalty regime (s 141E) imposes an additional civil penalty equal to the tax shortfall of the arrangement (up to NZ$50,000 minimum) on persons who promote, encourage, or assist in the avoidance arrangement. Late filing penalties and UOMI continue accruing until resolved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who are promoters or who knowingly participate face personal liability for the promoter penalty and the corporate shortfall penalty; no corporate veil protection is available. If the arrangement is a sham, the court may pierce the veil and hold directors personally liable to Inland Revenue for the entire reconstructed tax shortfall. Civil restitution routes include s 320 Companies Act 1993 misconduct proceedings, director disqualification orders, and contribution orders for company debts. Criminal charges for aiding a tax evasion may also carry imprisonment and travel bans pending trial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a specialty tea salon as a cash-intensive money-laundering conduit: accepting unreported cash payments in excess of NZ$10,000 without customer due diligence, deliberately structuring banking deposits into tranches below reporting thresholds ('smurfing'), processing credit-card or POS transactions without proper reconciliation, or allowing the CK_IC to receive wire transfers without any supporting commercial contract.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, a reporting entity that willfully fails to comply is liable on conviction to a civil fine or criminal penalty of up to NZ$2,000,000 for a body corporate and NZ$200,000 for an individual. Additional fines per violation can be imposed for each day of continued non-compliance. The Financial Markets Authority and the NZ Police Financial Intelligence Unit may seize cash and bank balances that are the proceeds of crime, and the Serious Fraud Office may prosecute for money laundering under s 243/243A of the Crimes Act 1961, with imprisonment up to 7 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers hold personal responsibility for establishing an AML/CFT compliance programme. They are individually liable for penalties up to NZ$200,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years for knowingly permitting money laundering. Directors may be disqualified from managing any risk-assessed business and banned from operating merchant facilities (POS/credit card rails). In serious cases, restraint orders and travel interdiction orders are issued to prevent the director leaving New Zealand while financial crime investigations are ongoing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Sham / No Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering the 'CK_IC' as an International Company with a 'Tax-Exempt Zone' status, but exercising all management, contractual decision-making, banking, and operational control from New Zealand; failing to register for New Zealand income tax, GST, and PAYE; or claiming treaty/tax-exempt status without any employees, physical premises, bank account, or real business activity in the Cook Islands.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The New Zealand tax residence rules (s YD 2, Income Tax Act 2007) treat a company as resident if it is incorporated in New Zealand or its centre of management is in New Zealand. A sham arrangement is void from the outset; the tea salon's profits are reassessed against the New Zealand operators at the 28% rate, with shortfall penalties of 20%–150%. Failure to register and file results in default assessments under s 106 and non-filer penalties of 20% of the shortage. In addition, the CFC rules (s CQ 2, EX 1–EX 21) may attribute income of the CK_IC to any New Zealand resident shareholder. The 'Tax-Exempt Zone' status of the Cook Islands entity provides no shield; New Zealand source income is always taxable in New Zealand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the sham IC face personal liability under s 372(1) of the Tax Administration Act 1994 for unpaid PAYE and GST; under s 370, directors are jointly and severally liable for the company's tax shortfall where the company was used to evade tax. A court may order civil restitution and the repayment of any distributions taken from the sham structure. Director disqualification orders under the Companies Act 1993 s 299 are routine. Travel bans (passport surrender and departure prohibition) are commonly imposed where the director retains offshore assets and faces a tax debt exceeding NZ$10,000, or where criminal charges for fraud are laid. Imprisonment of up to 5 years may be imposed for tax evasion; the court may also order personal contribution orders before discharging the company from liquidation.
